name: How to Get Startup Ideas
summary: Paul Graham's November 2012 essay: get startup ideas by looking for problems you have, not by trying to think of ideas.
description: The essay argues the best startup ideas are things the founders themselves want, can build and few others realize are worth doing. It covers why working on a problem you have matters, "made-up" sitcom ideas that sound plausible enough to fool you, and the narrow-but-deep "well" versus broad-and-shallow "crater" shapes of early markets.
